results.name: The 10 best AI BDRs in 2026
results.content:
Artisan's Ava is the best AI BDR (business development representative) in 2026: she is the only agent that owns every stage of the outbound job (sourcing, enrichment, multichannel outreach, reply handling, and booking) inside one platform, with autonomy you dial up or down. AiSDR and Amplemarket are the strongest alternatives. Most other tools cover part of the job.  
A BDR's job is outbound pipeline generation, nothing else. So this guide, updated July 2026, does something different from the usual listicle. It defines the AI BDR category, breaks the outbound job into the five stages an AI BDR must own, and ranks only outbound-capable platforms against one question: can it actually do the whole job?
## What is an AI BDR?  
An AI BDR is an AI agent that does the business development rep's job (generating outbound pipeline) instead of assisting a human who does it. Artisan coined the term's modern usage when it launched Ava, and the definitional guide lives here: what is an AI BDR. One test separates an AI BDR from AI-assisted software: if the agent disappeared tomorrow, would outbound stop, or would a human just lose a helper? A true AI BDR is accountable for meetings booked, not tasks completed.
## What changed in the AI BDR category in 2025-2026?  
- **Apollo bought Pocus**(March 19, 2026), pushing the biggest per-seat platform toward an "AI-native GTM OS" and signal-driven selling.
- **Salesforce closed its Qualified acquisition**(April 1, 2026), consolidating inbound agents into Agentforce and sharpening the inbound/outbound split this article ranks on.
- **11x reset its leadership**after TechCrunch's March 2025 reporting on misstated customers. CTO Prabhav Jain became CEO in May 2025.
- **New money chased the autonomous end:**Alta's $25 million Series A (July 8, 2026) and Monaco's $50M Series B led by Benchmark (May 2026) both back agents, not seat software.
- **Pricing moved toward usage and outcomes:**Salesforce shifted Agentforce to $0.10/action Flex Credits and HubSpot launched credit-based outcome pricing ($0.010 per credit) in April 2026. The market is converging on paying for work performed.

results.name: 11x vs. Alta: Which should you choose in 2026?
results.content:
## Key Takeaways  
- 11x has raised roughly $74M from investors including a16z and Benchmark, and runs Alice for multichannel outreach plus Julian, a named AI phone agent.
- Alta raised a $25M Series A in July 2026 and positions itself as an "AI GTM System of Actions," its label for a broad go-to-market (GTM) platform, with an SDR agent called Katie and AI calling.
- Alta claims SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance per its site. 11x is the more capital-heavy and channel-broad of the two.
- 11x drew documented scrutiny in 2025: TechCrunch reported customer claims it could not support (March 24, 2025), its founder-CEO stepped down to non-executive chairman in May 2025, and chief technology officer Prabhav Jain became CEO. Reviewers report deliverability and CRM-sync complaints.
- Neither publishes fully self-serve pricing, and both lean toward a sales conversation. 11x now publishes a Growth tier from $3,750/month billed annually (about $45K/year), with higher tiers custom, while Alta is gated on a "pay for what you use" model quoted by team size.
- Choose 11x for channel breadth and funding stability; choose Alta if you want a newer, leaner system and its security claims match your checklist.
## What should you know about each vendor's track record?  
For 11x, the record is documented and attributed. TechCrunch reported on March 24, 2025 that customers made performance claims the company could not support. In May 2025, its founder-CEO stepped down to non-executive chairman and chief technology officer Prabhav Jain became CEO. Reviewers have separately reported deliverability and CRM-sync complaints. 11x remains funded and active, but a multi-year commitment deserves eyes-open diligence.  
For Alta, there is simply not much record yet. It raised its Series A in July 2026 and claims SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance on its site, which are meaningful signals if verified during procurement. The honest limitation is that a young product has a thin history, so references, security documentation, and a trial matter more than usual before you commit.
### Can either tool replace a human SDR?  
Both automate large parts of the SDR job, but you still own targeting, data quality, and oversight. Treat them as tools that remove repetitive prospecting work rather than full replacements for a person. Our overview of what an AI BDR does explains where the automation stops and human judgment begins.
